info.description: This is an OpenAPI documentation generated automatically by Yedra.

Check if the user is authenticated.

orgId.description: The ID of the organization the user belongs to.

orgName.description: The name of the organization the user belongs to.

isOrgActive.description: Whether the organization has a valid subscription.

isOrgFrozen.description: Whether the organization has been suspended by a super-admin. When true the member has no API access at all and the client must route to the suspended screen — NOT to pricing, because no purchase clears it.

contractAwaitingApproval.description: True when this organization's term has ALREADY BEGUN but nobody has approved it, so it cannot activate. The member is not waiting for a date — they are waiting for a decision, and a countdown to a date in the past is the one thing the screen must not show them.

contractApproved.description: Whether oneAI has approved the term this organization is waiting for; present with `contractStartsAt`. An approved term whose start has passed is being switched on (the hourly activation has not run yet); an unapproved one whose start is ahead will not start on that date unless it is approved first. Each needs different words.

contractStartsAt.description: When this organization's contract term begins, present only while it is frozen BECAUSE it has not started. `frozen_at` carries two unrelated meanings and this is what tells them apart: with a date the member is waiting for a start, without one they were suspended. The two need opposite screens — a countdown and an apology are not interchangeable.

orgPlan.description: The pricing plan of the organization.

isAdmin.description: Whether the user is an admin of their organization.

seatTier.description: Which kind of seat this member holds. Orthogonal to orgPlan: the plan belongs to the organization, the tier to the person. `capabilities` below already has the tier floor applied, so a client does not need to combine the two itself.

isOrgFounder.description: True while the user is an admin and the organization's only member - i.e. they created it and nobody has joined yet. Onboarding reads it to tell creating an organization from joining one; it flips to false as soon as a second member exists.

personalSpace.description: The personal space ID of the user. NULL for a member with no personal workspace (the guest seat tier).

personalProject.description: The personal project ID of the user. NULL for a member with no personal workspace (the guest seat tier).

complianceEnabled.description: Whether compliance is enabled for the organization.

copilotEnabled.description: Whether the compliance copilot add-on is active for the organization.

unoEnabled.description: Whether the Uno assistant is enabled for the organization.

unoHintsEnabled.description: Whether Uno ambient education hints are enabled for the organization.

googleDriveEnabled.description: Whether the Google Drive space connector is enabled on this deployment (feature flag). When false, Google Drive is hidden from the space-connect wizard.

unconfiguredModels.description: Wire ids of the built-in chat models this deployment has no provider key for. They are left out of every model list; the admin model catalog hides them too.

modularProviders.description: The connector packages this deployment serves, each as the frontend needs it to draw and gate its spaces (`shared/sandboxed-providers.ts`). A package's provider exists only while it is here: its tile, label, icon and capabilities all come from this list, so they follow the install set rather than anything compiled into the frontend.

modularProvidersAwaitingOrgSetup.description: The connector packages among `modularProviders` whose required org-wide settings this organization's administrator has not saved yet. Nobody in the org can connect one until they are, so the connect wizard shows it disabled and says where the setting lives.

onboardingCompleted.description: Whether the user has completed onboarding.

firstname.description: The first name of the user (if onboarding completed).

lastname.description: The last name of the user (if onboarding completed).

jobIndustry.description: The job industry of the user (if onboarding completed).

jobPosition.description: The job position of the user (if onboarding completed).

preferredLanguage.description: The preferred language locale of the user.

preferredTheme.description: The preferred UI theme of the user.

suggestionsEnabled.description: Whether follow-up question suggestions are shown in chats.

chatMemoryEnabled.description: Whether saved standing preferences are applied to this user's chats.

showConnectSourceGallery.description: Whether the connector quick-start gallery is shown on the Spaces page.

uiPreferences.description: Per-user UI preferences, defaults applied. Written through PATCH /api/auth/preferences.

newsletterOptIn.description: Whether the user consents to receiving product updates and news by email.

newsletterFeatureEnabled.description: Whether this deployment has a newsletter (listmonk configured). When false, the opt-in is not offered.

lastSeenReleaseVersion.description: The version of the last release the user has acknowledged.

latestReleaseVersion.description: The current latest release version. Null if unreachable.

sessionExpiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the current session expires. Used by the frontend to proactively prompt re-authentication before the hard cutoff.

dailyLimitReached.description: Whether the user has spent their plan's daily LLM budget. Free plan only; always false on paid plans, which have no daily allowance.

usedPct.description: Percent of today's allowance already spent, 0-100 and clamped at 100. Deliberately a percentage rather than the underlying microcents: the raw figure is a provider cost we do not want to publish per-user, and a percentage is the only honest unit for an allowance shared across models with different prices.

resetsAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the next allowance reset. Computed server-side because the window is the UTC calendar day, which is 01:00/02:00 local for this product's German audience — the client must render this rather than assume its own midnight.

freeUsage.description: Today's allowance usage, or null on plans with no daily allowance. Lets the UI warn before the wall instead of only reporting it after.

creditBalanceMicro.description: Remaining credit pool balance in microcents (TEAM only).

quotaExhausted.description: Whether the user's model access is restricted due to quota/overage limits.

subscriptionStatus.description: Raw Stripe subscription_status (active, trialing, past_due, unpaid, canceled, etc.). Null for free plans.

isPartnerOrg.description: Whether the organization is reseller-managed by a partner (billing handled offline, no Stripe). True only for the 'reseller' billing relationship.

capabilities.description: The Layer-1 capabilities this user holds, resolved user > team > org_default. Lets an affordance react BEFORE the user reaches a screen that asks for input — a denied user previously filled in a whole connect wizard, credential included, and learned of the refusal only on submit. Any key an org has authored no explicit denial for reports true; org admins are resolved like everybody else, since the matrix binds them too. The server stays the authority — this payload never grants anything, it only lets the UI stop asking.

billingRelationship.description: How the org's billing is owned: 'direct' (self-serve, Stripe), 'reseller' (partner-managed, billed offline), or 'affiliate' (direct-Stripe org attributed to a partner).

post.summary: Remove a TOTP device.
Start device authorization for a desktop client.
post.description: Begins the device authorization flow (RFC 8628 style). The client generates a random secret locally, sends only its SHA-256 hash here, and keeps the raw secret to authenticate the later token poll. Returns the codes and the browser verification URL. No credential is ever placed in the URL.

secretHash.description: Base64 SHA-256 digest of the raw device secret. The raw secret is never sent here; it is replayed in the X-Device-Secret header on the token poll.

clientName.description: Human-readable client name shown on the approval screen.

deviceCode.description: Opaque code the client replays when polling for the token.

userCode.description: Short code the user enters in the browser.

verificationUri.description: Browser page where the user approves.

verificationUriComplete.description: Verification URL with the user code prefilled.

interval.description: Seconds to wait between token polls.

post.summary: Poll a device authorization for its session token.
post.description: Polled by the desktop client until the user approves in the browser. The raw device secret is sent in the X-Device-Secret header, never in the URL. Returns status 'pending' until approved, then 'complete' with a one-time session token.

parameters.name: x-device-secret
parameters.description: Raw device secret matching the secretHash sent to /device.

schema.description: Raw device secret matching the secretHash sent to /device.

token.description: Session token, present only when status is 'complete'.

post.summary: Approve a pending device authorization.
post.description: Called from the browser after the user confirms the code. Binds the device to the authenticated user. No token is minted here; the desktop client receives its session from the token poll, gated on the device secret only it holds.

requests.description: How many LLM requests this turn made. inputTokens is the SUM over all of them (each agentic iteration re-sends the conversation), which is why it can exceed contextTokens and the window itself.

contextTokens.description: How many tokens of the model's context window this conversation occupied at the end of the turn — the PROVIDER's own count for the last request's prompt, never an estimate. Distinct from inputTokens, which sums every call in the turn.

contextLimit.description: The context window of the model that answered, in tokens — the denominator for contextTokens.

outputTruncated.description: True when the model's output cap cut at least one request in this turn short, so the answer — or a tool call inside it — is shorter than the model intended. Read from the provider's own response envelope, never inferred from a token count. Absent on a clean turn and on every message persisted before this field existed.

timeline.description: Where the turn's wall-clock went: every model request, tool call and compaction in start order, in milliseconds since the turn started. firstOutputMs splits a model request into waiting (queueing, thinking) and generating. parentCallId marks a span that ran inside a subagent.

timelineOmitted.description: Spans that started after the timeline reached its cap and were not recorded.

usage.description: Display-only per-turn cost/token/duration summary for this assistant message. Computed off the billing path from the same usage + pricing the gateway billed. Present only on assistant messages produced after the feature landed.

autoRouted.description: True when Auto Routing chose this assistant message's model.

autoRoutingReason.description: Short justification from the Auto router, when available.

branches.description: List of branches that start at this message, i.e. alternatives to the current message. Also includes the currently selected branch ID.

userFeedback.description: The current user's feedback on this assistant message (null when not rated, undefined for user messages).

name.description: Full name, or the email when no name is set.

author.description: Who typed this message. Present on user messages sent after the feature landed, and on user messages backfilled from the chat's owner. Absent on assistant messages, and on the inherited half of a fork — `copyChat` copies history verbatim, so attributing it to the forker would be wrong.

placeholder.description: The token that replaced the span in the stored message.

patternTitle.description: Title of the pattern that triggered the redaction.

redactions.description: Compliance redactions applied to this user message. Present only when the message had sensitive spans replaced; lets the frontend restore the original text inline.

isBlocked.description: Whether the chat has been blocked due to compliance violations.

isOwner.description: Whether the current user may write this chat in place — owns it AND holds write on its project.

ownerName.description: Display name of `chats.user_id` — the one person who may append to this chat. Shown in the header when the reader is not that person.

canFork.description: Whether sending a message will copy the chat instead of appending to it. True for anyone who can read it but not write it.

forksToPersonalProject.description: Where a fork would land. TRUE when the caller cannot write the chat's project, so the copy goes to their own project rather than staying put — or, for a member who has none (the guest seat tier), the fork is refused. Meaningless unless `canFork`.

spaceId.description: The project the copy lives in.

myForks.description: Copies of THIS chat that the calling user already owns, newest first. Forking repeatedly is intended — but without this the user cannot see they have already done it, and makes another copy they did not mean to. Empty for a chat the caller has never forked, and for a chat that is not forkable.

isStreaming.description: Whether the chat currently has an active LLM stream.

suggestions.description: Follow-up question suggestions generated after the last assistant turn. Empty for chats that haven't produced a turn since the feature was added.

ragMode.description: Effective RAG mode for this chat after resolving F09 (org), F12 (org), and F12 project override. 'internal_only' is shown as a badge in the chat header.

get.summary: List the caller's pending AI edit suggestions for an artifact.
get.description:
Returns only suggestions that are PENDING, belong to the calling
user, and are visible on the branch their originating chat is currently on.

Branch visibility is a join rather than a stored flag: a suggestion records the
CHUNK it was produced in, and a chunk is inherited by every branch descended from
it, truncated at that branch's `up_to`. So editing a message away drops its
suggestions from the answer here, and paging back to the original branch brings
them back — with no delete path and nothing to keep in sync.

Unpaginated by design: the set is bounded by what one turn can propose against
one document, and the client renders all of it at once anyway.

patch.summary: Accept or reject one AI edit suggestion.
patch.description:
Records the caller's decision. Terminal and one-way: only a
PENDING suggestion can be resolved, and a resolved one cannot be reopened — a
reopen would let a later request re-offer a change the user already applied to the
document, which is the resurrection bug this table exists to prevent.

Accepting does NOT edit the document. The edit is a Yjs mutation the client makes
over the collab socket, which has its own write gate, and the client only records
the accept once the document has taken it. Recording it here as well would create
a second authority for one decision, free to disagree with the first.
